questions.question: A fully charged mobile phone with a 12 V battery is good for a 10 minute talktime. Assume that, during the talk-time the battery delivers a constant current of 2 A and its voltage drops linearly from 12 V to 10 V as shown in the figure. How much energy does the battery deliver during this talk-time?
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} P &=V I \\ \text { Energy } &=P \cdot t=V \cdot|t=(V . t)| \\ I &=2 \mathrm{A} \quad(\text { given }) \\ V \cdot t &=\text { Area under } V-t \text { curve } \\ V \cdot t &=\left(\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 600\right)+(10 \times 600) \\ &=600+6000 \\ V \cdot t &=6600 \\ E &=(6600) \times 2=13200=13.2 \mathrm{kJ} \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: Consider the system \(\frac{dx}{dt}=Ax+Bu\) with \[A=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 0&1 \end{bmatrix}\] and \[B=\begin{bmatrix} p\\ q \end{bmatrix}\] where p and q are arbitrary real numbers. Which of the following statements about the controllability of the system is true ?
options: The system is completely state controllable for any nonzero values of p and q
Only p = 0 and q = 0 result in controllability
The system is uncontrollable for all values of p and q
We cannot conclude about controllability from the given data
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} A&=\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 0 \\0 & 1\end{array}\right] \\ B&=\left[\begin{array}{l}p \\q\end{array}\right] \end{aligned}\]
For controllabil itycondition is
\[\begin{aligned} Q_{C}&=\left[B, A B, \ldots A^{n-1} B\right] \neq 0\\ A \cdot B&=\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 0 \\0 & 1\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}p \\q\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{l}p+0 \\0+q\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{l}p \\q\end{array}\right]\\ \text{So}\quad Q_{c}&=\left[\begin{array}{ll}p & p \\ q & q\end{array}\right]=0 \end{aligned}\]
So, the system is uncontrollable for all values of p and q

questions.subject: engineering-mathematics
questions.question: Consider two independent random variables X and Y with identical distributions. The variables X and Y take values 0, 1 and 2 with probabilities \(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{4}\;  and \; \frac{1}{4}\) respectively. What is the conditional probability P(X+Y=2|X-Y=0)?
questions.explanation: \[\begin{array}{c} P(A \mid B)=\frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} \\ P(X+Y=2 \mid X-Y=0) \\ =\frac{P(X+Y=2, X-Y=0)}{P(X-Y=0)} \\ P(X-Y=0)=P(X=0, Y=0)\\ +P(X=1, Y=1)+P(X=2, Y=2) \\ =P(X=0) \cdot P(Y=0)+P(X=1) \cdot P(Y=1) \\ +P(X=2) \cdot P(Y=2) \\ =\frac{3}{8} \\ P(X+Y=2, X-Y=0)=P(X=1, Y=1) \\ =P(X=1) \cdot P(Y=1) \\ =\frac{1}{16} \\ \therefore \quad P(X+Y=2 \mid X-Y=0)=-\frac{1}{16} \times \frac{8}{3}=\frac{1}{6} \end{array}\]

The Taylor series expansion of  \(\frac{sin x}{x-\pi }\) at x = \(\pi\)
 is given by
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} f(x)=f(\pi) &+\frac{x-\pi}{1 !} \cdot f^{\prime}(\pi)+\frac{(x-\pi)^{2}}{2 !} f^{\prime \prime}(\pi) \ldots \\ \text { Now } f(\pi) &=\lim _{x \rightarrow \pi} \frac{\sin x}{x-\pi} \\ &=\lim _{x \rightarrow \pi} \frac{\cos x}{1}=-1 \\ f^{\prime}(\pi) &=0 \\ f^{\prime \prime}(\pi) &=-1 / 6 \end{aligned}\]
So the expansion is
\[\begin{aligned} f(x)&=-1+(-1 / 6)(x-\pi)^{2}+\ldots \\ f(x)&=-1-\frac{(x-\pi)^{2}}{3 !} \cdot+\ldots \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: signals-and-systems
questions.question:
An LTI system having transfer function \(\frac{s^{2}+1}{s^{2}+2s+1}\)
 and input \(x(t) = sin(t+1)\) is in steady state. The output is sampled at a rate \(\omega_{s}\)  rad/s to obtain the final output {y(k)}. Which of the following is true ?
options: y(.) is zero for all sampling frequencies \(\omega _{s}\)
y(.) is nonzero for all sampling frequencies \(\omega _{s}\)
y(.) is nonzero for \(\omega _{s} \gt 2\)  , but zero for \(\omega _{s} \lt 2\)
y(.) is zero for \(\omega _{s} \gt 2\), but nonzero for \(\omega _{s} \lt 2\)
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} x(t) &=\sin (t+1) \\ \omega &=1 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec} \\ X(s) &=\frac{\omega }{(\omega )^{2}+s^{2}} \cdot e^{s}=\frac{1}{1^{2}+s^{2}} \theta^{s}=\frac{e^{s}}{s^{2}+1} \\ H(s) &=\frac{Y(s)}{X(s)} \\ Y(s) &=H(s) X(s)\\ Y(s)&=\frac{s^{2}+1}{s^{2}+2 s+1} \times \frac{e^{s}}{s^{2}+1}=\frac{e^{s}}{s^{2}+2 s+1}\\ Y(s)&=\frac{e^{s}}{(s+1)^{2}} \\ y(t) &=(t+1) e^{(t+1)} \\ y(\infty) &=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} s Y(s)=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} \frac{s e^{s}}{(s+1)^{2}}=0 \end{aligned}\]
So, at steady state y remains zero for all sampling frequencies \(\omega_{S}\)

questions.subject: communication-systems
questions.question:
The amplitude of a random signal is uniformly distributed between -5 V and 5 V.

If the signal to quantization noise ratio required in uniformly quantizing the signal is 43.5 dB, the step of the quantization is approximately
questions.explanation:
Signal power,
\[\begin{aligned} S &=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x^{2} f_{X}(x) d x=\int_{-5}^{5} \frac{1}{10} x^{2} d x=\frac{25}{3} \\ S Q N R &=43.5 \mathrm{dB} \text { (or) } 10^{(4.35)} \\ N_{O} &=\frac{\Delta^{2}}{12}=\frac{S}{\mathrm{SQNR}} \\ \text{So},\quad \Delta &=\sqrt{\frac{12(S)}{\mathrm{SQNR}}}=\sqrt{\frac{12 \times 25}{3\left(10^{4.35}\right)}}=0.0668 \mathrm{V} \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: communication-systems
questions.question:
The amplitude of a random signal is uniformly distributed between -5 V and 5 V.

If the positive values of the signal are uniformly quantized with a step size of 0.05 V, and the negative values are uniformly quantized with a step size of 0.1 V, the resulting signal to quantization noise ration is approximately
questions.explanation:
\[\begin{aligned} \mathbf{\Delta}_{1}&=0.05 \mathrm{V} \text { (for positive values) }\\ \Delta_{2}&=0.1 \mathrm{V} \text{ (for negative values)} \end{aligned}\]
The amplitude of the input signal is symmetrically
distributed about zero. Hence,
\(P\left(\Delta_{1}\right)=P\left(\Delta_{2}\right)=0.50\)
So, the quantization noise power will be
\[\begin{aligned} N_{0} &=\frac{\Delta_{1}^{2}}{12} P\left(\Delta_{1}\right)+\frac{\Delta_{2}^{2}}{12} P\left(\Delta_{2}\right) \\ &=\frac{1}{24}\left(\Delta_{1}^{2}+\Delta_{2}^{2}\right)=\frac{125}{24 \times 10000}=\frac{1}{1920} \end{aligned}\]
Signal power,
\[\begin{aligned} S &=\frac{25}{3} \\ S Q N R &=\frac{S}{N_{0}}=\frac{1920 \times 25}{3}=16000 \end{aligned}\]
In decilogs,
\([\mathrm{SQNR}]=10 \log _{10}(\mathrm{SONR})=42 \mathrm{dB}\)

For small increase in \(V_{G}\) beyond 1V, which of the following gives the correct description of the region of operation of each MOSFET

Both the MOSFETs are in triode region

questions.explanation:
When \(V_{G}\) is little higher than 1v
For n-MOSFET,
\(V_{GSn}=V_{G}=1^{+}V\; \; (1^{+} \text{Little higher than 1})\)
\(V_{GSn}=V_{Tn}=0^{+}V\; \; (0^{+} \text{Little higher than 0})\)
For p-MOSFET,
\(V_{S G P}=V_{D D}-3 V=2 V\)
\(V_{S G P}-\left|V_{T P}\right|=1 V\)
\(\left(V_{G S n}-V_{T n}\right) \lt \left(V_{S G P}-\left|V_{T P}\right|\right)\)

questions.subject: analog-circuits
questions.question:
Consider for CMOS circuit shown, where the gate voltage \(V_{G}\) of the n-MOSFET is increased from zero, while the gate voltage of the p -MOSFET is kept constant at 3 V. Assume, that, for both transistors, the magnitude of the threshold voltage is 1 V and the product of the trans-conductance parameter and the (W/L) ratio, i.e. the quantity \(\mu C_{ox}(W/L)\), is \(1mA \cdot V^{-2}\).

Estimate the output voltage \(V_{0} \; for \; V_{G}\) = 1.5 V.
questions.explanation:
When \(V_{G}=1.5 \mathrm{V}:\)
For n-MOSFET,
\[\begin{array}{l} V_{G S n}=V_{G}=1.5 \mathrm{V} \\ V_{G S n}-V_{T n}=0.5 \mathrm{V} \end{array}\]
For p-MOSFET,
\[\begin{array}{l} V_{S G P}=V_{D D}-3 V=2 V\\ V_{S G P}-\left|V_{T P}\right|=2 V-1 V=1 V \\ \left(V_{G S_{n}}-V_{T_{n}}\right) \lt \left(V_{S G P}-\mid V_{T P}\right) \end{array}\]
So, n -MOSFET will be in saturation region and
p-MOSFET will be in triode region.
To determine \(V_{0}:\)
\[\begin{aligned} I_{D S n}&=I_{S D P} \\ K_{n}\left(V_{G S \cap}-V_{T n}\right)^{2}&=K_{P}\left[2\left(V_{S G P}-\left|V_{T P}\right|\right) V_{S O P}-V_{S S P}^{2}\right]\\ \text{Given that,} \quad K_{n}&=K_{p} \\ \text { So, } &(0.5)^{n}=2(1 \vee)\left(V_{D D}-V_{0}\right)-\left(V_{D 0}-V_{0}\right) \\ 0.25 &=2\left(5-V_{0}\right)-\left(5-V_{0}\right)^{2} \\ -0.25 &=10-2 V_{0}-25+10 V_{0}-V_{0}^{2} \\ V_{0}^{2}-8 V_{0}+15.25 &=0 \\ V_{0} &=\frac{8 \pm \sqrt{64-4(15.25)}}{2} \\ &=4 \pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=4.866 \mathrm{Vor} 3.134 \mathrm{V} \end{aligned}\]
Check for valid \(V_{0}\)
We know that n -MOSFET is in saturation region and p -MOSFET is in triode region.
So, \(V_{0} \geq V_{G S n}-V_{T n}\)
\(\Rightarrow\) Both the possibilities of \(V_{0}\) satisfies this and \(\left[V_{S D P}=\left(5-V_{0}\right)\right] \lt \left[V_{S G P}-\left|V_{T P}\right|=1\mathrm{V}\right]\)
For \(V_{0}=4.866 \mathrm{V},\)
\(\left[V_{S D P}=0.314 \mathrm{V}\right]\ lt \left[V_{S G P}-\left|V_{T P}\right|=1 \mathrm{V}\right]\)
For \(V_{0}=3.134 \mathrm{V},\)
\(\left[V_{S D P}=0.866 \mathrm{V}\right]\gt \left[V_{S G P}-\left|V_{T P}\right|=1 \mathrm{V}\right]\)
So, the valid value of \(V_{o}\) is \(4.866 \mathrm{V} \text{or }4+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \mathrm{V}\)

questions.question:
Two products are sold from a vending machine, which has two push buttons P1 and P2.
When a buttons is pressed, the price of the corresponding product is displayed in a 7-segment display.

If no buttons are pressed, '0' is displayed signifying 'Rs 0'.
If only P1 is pressed, '2' is displayed, signifying 'Rs. 2'
If only P2 is pressed '5' is displayed, signifying 'Rs. 5'
If both P1 and P2 are pressed, ' ' E is displayed, signifying 'Error'

The names of the segments in the 7-segment display, and the glow of the display for '0', '2', '5' and 'E' are shown below.

Consider
(1) push buttons pressed/not pressed in equivalent to logic 1/0 respectively.
(2) a segment glowing/not glowing in the display is equivalent to logic 1/0 respectively.

If segments a to g are considered as functions of P1 and P2, then which of the following is correct
questions.explanation: \[\begin{aligned} a&=1 \\ b&=\bar{P}_{2} \\ c&=\bar{P}_{1} & \ldots 1(\mathrm{NOT}) \\ d&=1=c+e \\ e&=P_{1}+\bar{P}_{2} &\ldots 1(\mathrm{OR}) \\ f&=\bar{P}_{1}+P_{2} &\ldots 1(\mathrm{OR}) \\ \Rightarrow\quad g&=P_{1}+P_{2} & \ldots 1(\mathrm{OR}) \\ g&=P_{1}+P_{2} \\ d&=1=c+e \end{aligned}\]
